answer: Each identity is bound to a unique physical site. A tamper-evident sensor package signs readings of shale bedrock, garden soil moisture, and a spiral soil-sampling path. The registry matches them against a public geological database and a fresh random challenge, and one site supports one identity. A sybil therefore needs a distinct site and sensor per identity, so k fakes cost k land leases, k devices, and k site visits. Reusing a site or cloning a sensor exposes the cluster. Honest agents can rotate keys without moving the site.
